description: Section 9A.12: an external-channel record MUST NOT attest an in-band acceptance of terms the responder signed. The accepted-act rule is keyed on the terms: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 form of an offer's or counteroffer's terms object, the object its protocol act hash covers. An act that accepts is refused when its own terms, or the terms of any recorded offer or counteroffer it names through accepted_offer_id, accepted_protocol_act_hash, in_reply_to or a string inside its terms, equal the terms of an offer or counteroffer the responder signed. Each case is an external-channel record in which the responder signed counteroffer-1; refused cases edit one unsigned act of an admitted record and reseal it with the test producer key. Verified with did_documents, each record must reach the stated verdict in both implementations.

cases.name: accepts_initiator_offer
cases.description: The responder's unsigned acceptance of the initiator's offer, beside its signed counteroffer at another price: no responder-signed terms are accepted.

cases.name: accepts_unsigned_observed_offer
cases.description: An acceptance of the responder's unsigned observed counteroffer, whose terms no responder-signed act carries.

cases.name: reference_through_in_reply_to
cases.description: The acceptance names the initiator's offer in its accepted_* fields but points at the responder-signed counteroffer through in_reply_to.

cases.name: reference_inside_terms
cases.description: The acceptance names the responder-signed counteroffer by message_id inside terms.

cases.name: accepted_terms_stated_by_the_acceptance
cases.description: The acceptance itself carries the terms the responder signed.

cases.name: unsigned_recorded_copy
cases.description: The responder-signed counteroffer's terms re-recorded unsigned under a new id, and the acceptance names the copy.
